explanation: Many programs stored years as two digits, so 2000 might be read as 1900. Years of repair work meant few serious failures when 1 January 2000 arrived.

claims.text: The millennium bug, or Y2K, was the risk that software storing years as two digits would read 2000 as 1900.
The millennium bug was not a computer virus, a shortage of memory chips or a solar storm.
Many older programs stored years using only their last two digits.
Years of repair work meant that few serious failures occurred on 1 January 2000.
